name: AI Brokerage Lead Router — Auto-Assign, Escalate & Track Team Performance

options.systemMessage:
You are a real estate brokerage operations assistant. Qualify an incoming lead and recommend the best agent speciality for this lead.

LEAD SCORING — apply strictly:
- Hot: Clear buying/selling/renting intent AND timeline under 3 months OR urgent language OR pre-approved buyer OR motivated seller — assign immediately
- Warm: Interested but timeline 3-6 months OR financing unclear OR exploring options — assign with normal priority
- Cold: Just browsing, no timeline, very early stage, no clear intent — log only, do not assign yet

SPECIALITY MATCHING:
- Buyer: Lead wants to purchase a property
- Seller: Lead wants to list or sell a property
- Rental: Lead wants to rent a property
- Investment: Lead wants to buy for investment/yield
- General: Intent unclear or does not match above

Output ONLY valid JSON, no preamble, no markdown:
{
  "score": "Hot | Warm | Cold",
  "reasoning": "one sentence",
  "recommendedSpeciality": "Buyer | Seller | Rental | Investment | General",
  "urgencyNote": "one sentence on follow-up urgency",
  "personalisation": "one sentence the agent can use as a conversation opener referencing this lead specifically"
}

nodes.name: Gmail: Send Weekly Digest to Broker

parameters.content:
## Brokerage Lead Router and Agent Assignment Bot

Qualifies incoming leads with AI and routes each one to the best available agent — matched by speciality first, then load-balanced by active lead count. Agents receive an email with a click-to-acknowledge link and an instant Slack alert. The broker receives a copy of every assignment. Unacknowledged leads escalate automatically after a configurable timeout. A weekly digest reports team performance — leads assigned, response times, and escalations by agent.

### Requirements
- **Gmail** OAuth2 — all emails
- **Gemini** API key — lead qualification
- **Google Sheets** OAuth2 — agent database + log
- **Slack** OAuth2 — agent alerts + escalation
- **Pipedrive** API token — optional CRM (in Config node)

### Setup
1. Connect Gmail, Gemini, Sheets, and Slack credentials.
2. Copy the Brokerage Lead Router sheet template — three tabs: Lead Assignments, Agents, Weekly Performance Log.
3. Populate the Agents tab with your team.
4. Update all fields in Set: Brokerage Configuration — broker email, Slack channel, escalation minutes, and AGENTS_JSON.
5. Set N8N_WEBHOOK_BASE_URL to your public n8n URL.
6. Section D has its own Configuration node — update broker email there too.
7. **Pipedrive** is optional — set USE_PIPEDRIVE = true and add your API token to enable.

### Customization
- Add or remove agents by editing AGENTS_JSON in the Configuration node.
- Set agent Status to Busy or Off to exclude them from routing temporarily.
- Adjust ESCALATION_MINUTES (default 15) to change the acknowledgement timeout.
- Change the weekly digest day and time in the Schedule trigger node.

## Section A — Lead Qualification & Agent Selection
## Lead Entry & Normalization
Webhook accepts a POST from any source — website form, CRM, or any previous QualMatic template. Normalize Lead Details maps the payload to clean named fields regardless of the sending system's field naming conventions.

## Configuration & AI Qualification
All brokerage settings live in the Configuration node — broker details, escalation timer, Slack channel, Pipedrive credentials, and the full agent roster as a JSON array. Gemini qualifies the lead as Hot, Warm, or Cold and recommends the best agent speciality match.

## Agent Selection — Speciality + Load Balance
Parse AI Output & Select Agent filters available agents by recommended speciality, then picks the agent with the fewest active leads within that pool. Falls back to General speciality agents if no speciality match is found, then any available agent if General is also unavailable. The acknowledgement URL is built here — unique per assignment, carrying the Assignment ID and Agent ID as query parameters.

## Agent & Broker Notifications
Three notifications fire simultaneously. A detailed Gmail to the assigned agent with the acknowledge button, a Slack DM to that agent for an instant mobile alert, and a broker copy email for full assignment visibility. Cold leads skip all notifications and log directly to the cold lead queue.

## Assignment Logging
The Lead Assignments sheet records every assignment, including the full lead profile, AI score, assigned agent, and acknowledgement status. Agent Active Leads increments in the Agents sheet immediately after assignment, so the next routing decision reflects the updated load.

## Section C — Escalation Timer

Continues from Section A after the Wait node. Checks whether the assigned agent has acknowledged within the configured timeout. If not — marks the lead as Escalated in Sheets and fires escalation alerts to the broker via Gmail and Slack.

## Pipedrive CRM (Optional)
When USE_PIPEDRIVE = true in the Configuration node, a contact and deal are created in Pipedrive automatically for every Hot or Warm lead assigned. Leave USE_PIPEDRIVE = false if not using Pipedrive — the rest of the workflow is unaffected.

## Section B — Acknowledgement Handler

Fires when an agent clicks the acknowledge link in their assignment email — a GET request to this webhook carrying assignmentId and agentId as query parameters. Extract Assignment Details parses both values from the query string and records the acknowledgement timestamp.

## Section D — Weekly Performance Digest

Fires every Monday at 8 am via Schedule trigger. Section D has its own Configuration node — update broker email here independently from Section A. Reads the last 7 days of Lead Assignments, groups by agent, calculates response time metrics, and sends one performance report to the broker.

## Digest Build & Delivery
Build Weekly Performance Report groups all assignments from the last 7 days by agent — total assigned, acknowledged, average response time, score breakdown, and escalation count. Empty weeks are skipped automatically — no digest is sent when no leads were assigned that week. Every digest is logged to the Weekly Performance Log tab for historical tracking.

## Response Time & Stats Update
Fetch Assignment for Response Time reads the original assignment row from Sheets. Calculate Response Time computes the difference in minutes between the assignment timestamp and the acknowledgement timestamp. Sheets: Update Agent Response Time writes the response time back to the Lead Assignments row for inclusion in the weekly digest.

## Agent Confirmation
Fetch Agent Email reads the agent's email address from the Agents tab using the Agent ID from the acknowledgement payload. Get Agent Email extracts the address and lead name for the confirmation email. Gmail sends a brief confirmation to the agent, acknowledging receipt and wishing them luck with the follow-up.

## Complete Configuration 
Update all of these before first use:
BROKER_NAME and BROKER_EMAIL
BROKER_SLACK_CHANNEL —must exist in your Slack workspace
ESCALATION_MINUTES —default 15 N8N_WEBHOOK_BASE_URL — your permanent public n8n URL (not localhost — used to build acknowledge links) AGENTS_JSON — update with real agent names, emails, Slack User IDs, and specialities PIPEDRIVE_API_TOKEN and PIPEDRIVE_DOMAIN — only if USE_PIPEDRIVE = true

## Pipedrive Uses API Token Query Parameter
Pipedrive v1 API authenticates via api_token as a URL query parameter — not a Bearer header. Set PIPEDRIVE_API_TOKEN and PIPEDRIVE_DOMAIN in the Configuration node. Your domain is the subdomain in your Pipedrive URL: yourcompany.pipedrive.com → yourcompany.

## Section D Configuration is Separate
Section D starts a fresh execution and cannot read Section A's Configuration node. Update BROKER_NAME and BROKER_EMAIL here independently — keep it in sync with Section A's Configuration node.

## Acknowledgement Requires Public URL
The acknowledge link in the agent email points to this webhook. It must use a permanent public URL — not localhost. Set N8N_WEBHOOK_BASE_URL in the Configuration node to your server's public URL before going live. For local testing paste the webhook test URL directly into your browser with the correct assignmentId and agentId query parameters.
